content: Yama niyama asana pranayama pratyahara dharana dhyana samadhayo ashtav angani. (The eight limbs of yoga are ethical restraint, personal observances, steady posture, breath regulation, sensory withdrawal, concentration, meditation, and absorption).
author: Patanjali
explanation:
In the profound psychology of the Yoga Sutras, Patanjali outlines the systematic roadmap for stilling mental fluctuations into radiant, sovereign stillness.

This teaching (Yama niyama asana pranayama pratyahara dharana dhyana samadh...) focuses directly on yama and niyama. When we clear away reactive illusions and anchor ourselves in timeless principles, the mind recovers its pristine clarity and inner resilience.

True realization is never an abstract intellectual debate—it is an active discipline lived through quiet integrity and conscious presence in everyday moments.
practicalInsight: Apply this teaching on yama today: take a deliberate pause before reacting, align your actions with quiet integrity, and refuse to let transient friction disturb your center.
reflectionPrompt: How can you embody deeper yama and niyama in the primary challenge you are navigating right now?
